title: Filter-Free Indistinguishable Photon Generation from Continuous-Wave-Driven Integrated Microresonators
authors: Ruiyang Chen, Sicheng Zeng, Yuan Chen, Sanli Huang, Zeying Zhong, Zhen Chen, Xue Bai, Yi-Han Luo, Junqiu Liu
abstract: Quantum networks require scalable photon sources combining narrow linewidth, high efficiency, and high indistinguishability. Microresonator photon-pair sources are promising candidates, yet a source-only description based on the joint spectral amplitude (JSA) predicts near-zero Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference visibility between photons generated by independent, CW-driven microresonators. In this work, we show that the observed HOM interference is not determined by the JSA alone. By combining finite-time detection with cavity-enhanced spontaneous four-wave mixing, we characterize a detector-conditioned heralded state governed by the idler-photon detection window. We further demonstrate that independently optimizing the idler and signal detection windows allows both heralded-photon indistinguishability and intrinsic heralding efficiency to approach unity, without spectral filtering or complex source engineering. Utilizing integrated high-$Q$ silicon nitride microresonators, we achieve HOM visibilities of 0.992(8) and 0.942(12), without background subtraction, at fourfold count rates of 4.5(3) and 12.2(6) Hz, respectively. Our work establishes CW-driven high-$Q$ microresonators as a robust and scalable platform for quantum-network primitives.
summary: This paper presents an experimental demonstration of generating highly indistinguishable photon pairs using integrated silicon nitride microresonators pumped by a continuous-wave laser. By developing and implementing a double-window coincidence detection scheme, the authors overcome theoretical limitations that previously predicted poor performance. This establishes CW-driven high-Q resonators as a robust and scalable platform for quantum network applications.
main_problem: The primary challenge is generating scalable, high-indistinguishability photon sources required for quantum networks, as conventional theory predicts poor Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference visibility from independent continuous-wave (CW)-driven microresonators.
main_result: The authors demonstrated that by employing a detector-conditioned heralded state approach, they achieved high HOM visibilities (e.g., 0.992) and near-unity indistinguishability and heralding efficiency without spectral filtering.
method: The work moves beyond source-only descriptions by analyzing the system using finite-time detection logic, specifically implementing a double-window coincidence detection scheme.
model_or_system: The experiment utilizes integrated high-Q silicon nitride microresonators pumped by a CW laser, generating photon pairs via cavity-enhanced spontaneous four-wave mixing. The setup involves complex on-chip routing, interferometry, and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs).
key_observables: HOM visibility (V), detector-conditioned purity (P), and intrinsic heralding efficiency ($\eta$).
important_parameters: High-Q silicon nitride platform, CW pumping, double-window coincidence logic, and specific count rates (e.g., 4.5 Hz).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a flat spectral acceptance window bandwidth B >> $\kappa$, and the key technical advancement relies on decoupling the purity and efficiency measurements via double-window logic.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the failure of the JSA model for CW sources, show how P and $\eta$ approach unity by optimizing detection windows ($T$ and $T'$), and detail the comparison between single-window and double-window coincidence logic.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the theoretical limitation of source-only descriptions. It then introduces the detector-conditioned state formalism. The experimental section details the $	ext{Si}_3	ext{N}_4$ chip fabrication and setup. The core argument is built by comparing the performance under single-window versus the superior performance achieved using double-window coincidence logic.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial experimental blueprint for realizing quantum network primitives using integrated photonics, directly addressing the scalability and performance limitations inherent in CW-driven sources, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and quantum information.
